[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is called electronegativity?","marks":1,"answer":"Electronegativity is a fundamental chemical property that measures how strongly an atom attracts shared electrons when it forms a chemical bond with another atom. To understand this simply, imagine two atoms sharing a pair of electrons. If one atom pulls the shared electrons closer to itself, it has higher electronegativity. This attraction occurs because atoms with more protons in their nucleus exert a stronger pull on the negatively charged electrons. In short, electronegativity is the "tug-of-war" ability of an atom within a covalent bond.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Galena is the ore of lead–Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Ore vs. Mineral Explanation: Naturally occurring solid substances found in the Earth’s crust are called minerals. However, not all minerals are economically useful. An ore is specifically a type of mineral from which a valuable metal can be extracted profitably and conveniently on a large scale. Galena has the chemical formula \( PbS \) (lead sulfide). It is classified as an ore of lead because it contains a high percentage of lead metal, and the process to extract lead from galena is cost-effective, energy-efficient, and widely established in the metallurgical industry. Therefore, galena is not just any lead-containing rock; it is the primary commercial source of lead.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the causes why the produced gaseous element of reaction-(i) is placed in group-1 of periodic table.","marks":3,"answer":"Hydrogen Placement in Group-1 Analysis:
Reaction (i) produces hydrogen gas (\( H_2 \)) as the gaseous element. Hydrogen is a unique non-metal, yet it is traditionally placed at the very top of group-1 in the periodic table, directly above the alkali metals like Lithium (\( Li \)), Sodium (\( Na \)), and Potassium (\( K \)). This placement is logical for beginners to understand when we look at electron configuration:
Hydrogen has an atomic number of 1, meaning its electron configuration is \( 1s^1 \). Just like alkali metals, hydrogen possesses exactly one electron in its outermost shell. This single valence electron allows hydrogen to lose one electron to form a \( H^+ \) ion, behaving similarly to how alkali metals form \( M^+ \) ions. Additionally, hydrogen shares other key traits with group-1 elements: it acts as a strong reducing agent, it combines with halogens to form binary compounds (like \( HCl \), similar to \( NaCl \)), and it forms ionic hydrides with highly electropositive metals. Although hydrogen can also gain an electron to form \( H^- \) (like halogens), its overall chemical behavior, ionization energy trend, and electron loss tendency align most closely with the alkali metals. Hence, it is placed in group-1.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the dehydrating and oxidation properties of X compound of the stem.","marks":4,"answer":"Analysis of Compound X (\( H_2SO_4 \)):
Completing reaction (ii) gives us:
\( H_2S_2O_7 + H_2O \rightarrow 2H_2SO_4 \)
Therefore, compound X is sulfuric acid (\( H_2SO_4 \)), a vital industrial chemical known for both its strong oxidizing and dehydrating abilities.
Oxidizing Property:
Concentrated \( H_2SO_4 \) is a powerful oxidizing agent because it readily gives up oxygen atoms (\( [O] \)) during chemical reactions. When it oxidizes another substance, it gets reduced to sulfur dioxide (\( SO_2 \)) and water. For example, when copper metal reacts with hot, concentrated sulfuric acid:
\( H_2SO_4 (\text{conc}) \rightarrow H_2O (l) + SO_2 (g) + [O] \)
\( Cu(s) + [O] \rightarrow CuO(s) \)
\( CuO(s) + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow CuSO_4 (aq) + H_2O (l) \)
\( Cu(s) + 2H_2SO_4 (\text{conc}) \rightarrow CuSO_4 (aq) + SO_2 (g) + 2H_2O (l) \)
Here, copper loses electrons (oxidized), while sulfuric acid gains electrons and is reduced. This same oxidizing behavior applies to other metals like zinc, iron, and aluminum.
Dehydrating Property:
\( H_2SO_4 \) has an extremely strong affinity for water molecules. It can forcibly remove hydrogen and oxygen atoms in a 2:1 ratio (exactly as they appear in water) from organic compounds. This process is called dehydration. A classic demonstration involves adding concentrated sulfuric acid to table sugar (sucrose):
\( C_{12}H_{22}O_{11} (s) + \text{conc. } H_2SO_4 \rightarrow 12C (s) + 11H_2O \)
The water molecules are instantly absorbed by the acid, leaving behind a porous, black mass of carbon. The absorbed water then hydrates the sulfuric acid itself, releasing significant heat. This extreme ability to strip water makes \( H_2SO_4 \) an essential drying agent and a key reagent in organic synthesis.
---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is sub-metal?","marks":1,"answer":"Sub-metal (more commonly known as a metalloid or semi-metal) refers to elements that exhibit a blend of both metallic and non-metallic properties. These elements are found along the zigzag line on the right side of the periodic table. For example, they may look shiny like metals but are brittle and conduct electricity only partially (semiconductors). Classic examples include Silicon (\( Si \)) and Arsenic (\( As \)).","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why is lime applied to an ant bite wound?","marks":2,"answer":"Lime on Ant Bites: When an ant bites or stings, it injects methanoic acid (formic acid, \( HCOOH \)) into the skin, which causes intense burning and pain. Lime, or calcium hydroxide (\( Ca(OH)_2 \)), is a mild base (alkali). When applied to the wound, it undergoes a neutralization reaction with the injected acid. The base cancels out the acid's effect, forming a harmless salt and water, which instantly relieves pain and reduces inflammation:
\( 2HCOOH + Ca(OH)_2 \rightarrow (HCOO)_2Ca + 2H_2O \)
This simple acid-base reaction is why a paste of lime or baking soda is a traditional and effective home remedy for insect stings.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the extraction of desired metal from compound ‘X’.","marks":3,"answer":"Extraction of Copper from Compound X:
In the given reaction, Chalcocite (\( Cu_2S \)) reacts with oxygen to form Copper(I) oxide (\( X = Cu_2O \)) and Sulfur dioxide gas (\( Y = SO_2 \)):
\( 2Cu_2S + 3O_2 \rightarrow 2Cu_2O + 2SO_2 \)
To extract pure copper metal from \( Cu_2O \), a process called self-reduction is used. The remaining unreacted chalcocite (\( Cu_2S \)) acts as the reducing agent for the copper oxide. No external carbon is needed. The chemical process is straightforward:
\( Cu_2S + 2Cu_2O \rightarrow 6Cu + SO_2 \)
The molten copper produced is called blister copper (about 98% pure). To reach 99.99% purity, it undergoes electrolytic refining. In this step, impure copper acts as the anode, pure copper acts as the cathode, and a solution of \( CuSO_4 \) and dilute \( H_2SO_4 \) acts as the electrolyte. When electricity passes through:
At the anode: \( Cu \rightarrow Cu^{2+} + 2e^- \)
At the cathode: \( Cu^{2+} + 2e^- \rightarrow Cu \)
Impurities like gold and silver settle at the bottom as anode mud, while pure copper deposits on the cathode.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Is it possible to prepare oxidizing and dehydrating acid from compound ‘Y’? Analyze with reaction.","marks":4,"answer":"Preparation of Oxidizing/Dehydrating Acid from Y:
Compound Y is sulfur dioxide (\( SO_2 \)). It is absolutely possible to convert \( SO_2 \) into sulfuric acid (\( H_2SO_4 \)), which is both a strong oxidizing agent and a powerful dehydrating agent. This is done through the Contact Process, which occurs in three main stages:
Stage 1: \( SO_2 \) is catalytically oxidized to sulfur trioxide (\( SO_3 \)) using vanadium pentoxide (\( V_2O_5 \)) at \( 450^\circ C \):
\( 2SO_2(g) + O_2(g) \xrightarrow{V_2O_5, 450^\circ C} 2SO_3(g) \)
Stage 2: Directly adding water to \( SO_3 \) creates a dangerous, unmanageable fog. Instead, \( SO_3 \) is dissolved in concentrated sulfuric acid to form oleum (fuming sulfuric acid):
\( H_2SO_4(l) + SO_3(g) \rightarrow H_2S_2O_7(l) \)
Stage 3: Oleum is carefully diluted with water to produce pure, concentrated sulfuric acid:
\( H_2S_2O_7(l) + H_2O(l) \rightarrow 2H_2SO_4(l) \)
The final product, \( H_2SO_4 \), acts as a strong dehydrating agent (removes water from compounds) and an oxidizing agent (releases atomic oxygen), making it one of the most versatile industrial chemicals.
---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is called homologous series?","marks":1,"answer":"A homologous series is a family of organic compounds that share the same general formula, similar chemical properties, and the same functional group. Each successive member in the series differs by a \( -CH_2- \) unit (methylene group). Because they share a core structure, they undergo similar reactions, but their physical properties (like boiling point) change gradually as molecular size increases.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Same empirical formula can be for different compounds–Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Identical Empirical Formulas:
The empirical formula shows only the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a compound, not the actual number of atoms. Therefore, completely different molecules with varying sizes and molecular masses can share the same empirical formula. For instance, Acetylene (\( C_2H_2 \)) and Benzene (\( C_6H_6 \)) are vastly different compounds. Acetylene is a linear gas used in welding, while benzene is a cyclic liquid solvent. However, both have a carbon-to-hydrogen ratio of \( 1:1 \). When simplified, both empirical formulas become \( CH \). This proves that the empirical formula alone cannot distinguish between different molecular compounds.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Give the comparative description of diffusion rate of ‘M’ and ‘T’ gases.","marks":3,"answer":"Diffusion Rate Comparison of M and T:
From the reactions:
(i) \( S + O_2 \rightarrow SO_2 \) (Gas M)
(ii) \( N_2 + 3H_2 \rightarrow 2NH_3 \) (Gas T)
So, M is Sulfur Dioxide (\( SO_2 \)) and T is Ammonia (\( NH_3 \)).
Diffusion is the spontaneous spreading of gas molecules from an area of high concentration to low concentration. According to Graham's Law of Diffusion, the rate of diffusion is inversely proportional to the square root of the gas's molar mass. Lighter gases diffuse faster.
Molar mass of \( SO_2 = 32 + (16 \times 2) = 64 \text{ g/mol} \)
Molar mass of \( NH_3 = 14 + (1 \times 3) = 17 \text{ g/mol} \)
Since \( NH_3 \) is significantly lighter, it diffuses much faster than \( SO_2 \). The mathematical ratio is:
\( \frac{\text{Rate}_{NH_3}}{\text{Rate}_{SO_2}} \)
\( = \sqrt{\frac{M_{SO_2}}{M_{NH_3}}} \)
\( = \sqrt{\frac{64}{17}} \)
\( \approx 1.94 \)
This means ammonia diffuses nearly twice as fast as sulfur dioxide under identical conditions.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Oleum can be prepared from ‘M’ gas–Analyze.","marks":4,"answer":"Oleum Preparation from M Gas:
Gas M is \( SO_2 \). Oleum (\( H_2S_2O_7 \)) can indeed be manufactured from \( SO_2 \) through industrial catalytic oxidation. First, purified \( SO_2 \) is mixed with excess oxygen and passed over a vanadium pentoxide (\( V_2O_5 \)) catalyst at \( 400-500^\circ C \). This converts it to sulfur trioxide:
\( 2SO_2(g) + O_2(g) \rightarrow 2SO_3(g) \)
Instead of dissolving \( SO_3 \) directly in water, it is absorbed into \( 98\% \) concentrated sulfuric acid. This absorption reaction produces oleum:
\( H_2SO_4(l) + SO_3(g) \rightarrow H_2S_2O_7(l) \)
Oleum is a stable, fuming liquid that can be safely transported. When diluted with a precise amount of water, it yields pure concentrated sulfuric acid. This indirect method prevents the formation of corrosive sulfuric acid mist and ensures safe, efficient industrial production.
---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is research?","marks":1,"answer":"Research is a systematic, organized, and scientific process of investigating existing knowledge, conducting experiments, collecting data, and analyzing results to discover new facts, solve problems, or develop new theories. It follows a structured methodology to ensure findings are reliable, reproducible, and evidence-based.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Which one will be evaporated first from the mixture of iodine and edible salt when the temperature of the mixture is increased?","marks":2,"answer":"Sublimation Separation: Iodine (\( I_2 \)) will evaporate first. Iodine is a sublimable solid, meaning it transitions directly from solid to gas when heated, without passing through a liquid phase. Common salt (\( NaCl \)) has a very high melting point and does not sublimate under normal heating conditions. Therefore, when the mixture is gently warmed, iodine vaporizes instantly, leaving the salt behind. The iodine vapor can later be condensed on a cool surface to recover it in pure form.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Determine the molecular formula of the hydrocarbon.","marks":3,"answer":"Molecular Formula Calculation:
We start by finding the mass ratio of Carbon and Hydrogen:
Carbon percentage = \( 80\% \)
Hydrogen percentage = \( 100\% - 80\% = 20\% \)
Now, we calculate the mole ratio using atomic masses (\( C=12 \), \( H=1 \)):
Moles of C = \( 80 / 12 \)
\( \approx 6.67 \)
Moles of H = \( 20 / 1 \)
\( = 20 \)
Dividing both by the smallest number (6.67) gives a simple ratio:
C : H = \( 6.67 / 6.67 \) : \( 20 / 6.67 \)
\( = 1 : 3 \)
So, the empirical formula is \( CH_3 \).
Empirical formula mass = \( 12 + (3 \times 1) = 15 \)
Given molecular mass = 30
We find the multiplier \( n \):
\( n = 30 / 15 \)
\( = 2 \)
Therefore, molecular formula = \( (CH_3)_2 = C_2H_6 \) (Ethane).","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Describe the metal extraction process from the ore of the scenario-B of the stem.","marks":4,"answer":"Aluminum Extraction from Bauxite:
Bauxite (\( Al_2O_3 \cdot 2H_2O \)) is the primary ore of aluminum. Extracting aluminum is a two-stage industrial process because aluminum is highly reactive and cannot be reduced by carbon.
Step 1: Purification (Bayer’s Process): Raw bauxite contains impurities like iron oxide and silica. It is digested with hot, concentrated sodium hydroxide (\( NaOH \)). Aluminum oxide dissolves to form sodium aluminate, while impurities remain solid and are filtered out. The solution is then cooled and seeded with \( Al(OH)_3 \), causing pure aluminum hydroxide to precipitate. Heating this precipitate yields pure alumina (\( Al_2O_3 \)).
Step 2: Electrolytic Reduction (Hall-Héroult Process): Pure \( Al_2O_3 \) has a very high melting point, so it is dissolved in molten cryolite (\( Na_3AlF_6 \)), which lowers the melting temperature and improves conductivity. The mixture is placed in a steel cell with carbon electrodes. When direct current is passed:
At cathode (negative): \( Al^{3+} + 3e^- \rightarrow Al(l) \) (Molten aluminum sinks to the bottom)
At anode (positive): \( 2O^{2-} \rightarrow O_2(g) + 4e^- \)
The oxygen reacts with the carbon anode to form \( CO_2 \). This continuous electrolytic process produces 99% pure liquid aluminum, which is tapped and cast into ingots.
---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is paraffin?","marks":1,"answer":"Paraffin is a soft, white or colorless waxy solid derived primarily from petroleum, coal, or oil shale. Chemically, it consists of straight-chain saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes) with high molecular weights (typically \( C_{20} \) to \( C_{40} \)). It is chemically inert, water-resistant, and has a low melting point, making it ideal for candles, coatings, lubricants, and cosmetic products.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Neutralization reaction is a non-redox reaction–Explain it.","marks":2,"answer":"Neutralization as Non-Redox: A neutralization reaction occurs when an acid and a base react to form salt and water. For example:
\( HCl + NaOH \rightarrow NaCl + H_2O \)
In this process, the hydrogen ion (\( H^+ \)) from the acid simply combines with the hydroxide ion (\( OH^- \)) from the base. No electrons are transferred between atoms; oxidation states of all elements remain unchanged before and after the reaction. Since oxidation and reduction require a change in oxidation numbers (electron transfer), neutralization is classified as a non-redox reaction.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the purification process of metal mentioned in the stem one.","marks":3,"answer":"Zinc Purification Process:
The metal in question is Zinc, extracted from Zinc Blende (\( ZnS \)). First, \( ZnS \) is roasted in excess air to convert it to zinc oxide (\( ZnO \)):
\( 2ZnS + 3O_2 \rightarrow 2ZnO + 2SO_2 \)
The \( ZnO \) is then mixed with powdered coke (carbon) and heated in a fireclay retort at around \( 1200^\circ C \). Carbon reduces the oxide:
\( ZnO + C \rightarrow Zn + CO \)
Zinc vaporizes at this temperature and passes through a clay condenser pipe. As it cools, it liquefies and collects in receivers. However, this crude zinc still contains impurities like lead, iron, and cadmium. To purify it further, fractional distillation or electrolytic refining is used. In electrolytic refining, impure zinc acts as the anode, pure zinc as the cathode, and zinc sulfate solution as the electrolyte. Pure zinc deposits on the cathode, yielding 99.95% pure zinc.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"For the preparation of compound ‘C’, process (ii) is more preferable than process (i) in the stem–Put your opinion in favour of it.","marks":4,"answer":"Preference for Process (ii) in Acid Preparation:
Assuming compound C is sulfuric acid (\( H_2SO_4 \)), and process (i) is direct hydration of \( SO_3 \), while process (ii) is the oleum method:
Process (i): \( SO_3(g) + H_2O(l) \rightarrow H_2SO_4(aq) \)
Process (ii): \( SO_3(g) + H_2SO_4(l) \rightarrow H_2S_2O_7(l) \) followed by \( H_2S_2O_7(l) + H_2O(l) \rightarrow 2H_2SO_4(l) \)
Process (ii) is vastly preferred for two critical reasons:
1. Safety and Heat Management: The direct reaction of \( SO_3 \) with water is extremely violent and highly exothermic. It instantly produces a dense, corrosive fog of sulfuric acid aerosols that are dangerous to workers and equipment, and nearly impossible to condense into liquid acid.
2. Yield and Control: Absorbing \( SO_3 \) in concentrated \( H_2SO_4 \) to form oleum is a smooth, controllable, and safe process. The resulting oleum is stable for transport. When carefully diluted with a calculated amount of water, it produces pure, concentrated sulfuric acid without forming corrosive mists. This indirect method maximizes yield, ensures industrial safety, and guarantees product quality.
---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is called methylated spirit?","marks":1,"answer":"Methylated spirit (also known as denatured alcohol) is a mixture of ethanol (about 90-95%) with a small percentage of toxic methanol (5-10%) and sometimes additives like pyridine or dyes. The methanol makes it poisonous and unfit for human consumption, which prevents its illegal taxation as a beverage. It is widely used as a solvent, fuel for spirit lamps, cleaning agent, and in laboratories.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why pure H₂SO₄ doesn’t act as an acid? Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Acidity of Pure Sulfuric Acid: An acid is defined by the Arrhenius theory as a substance that produces hydrogen ions (\( H^+ \)) or hydronium ions (\( H_3O^+ \)) when dissolved in water. Pure (100%) sulfuric acid is a covalent molecular liquid. Without water molecules present, there is no medium to accept protons and form \( H_3O^+ \) ions. Ionization cannot occur in the absence of a solvent. Therefore, in its pure, anhydrous state, \( H_2SO_4 \) does not dissociate into ions and cannot exhibit acidic behavior. It only acts as an acid when dissolved in water.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Describe the condensation process of the Ore of element ‘C’ of the stem.","marks":3,"answer":"Condensation of Galena (Ore of C):
Element C is Lead (\( Pb \)), and its ore is Galena (\( PbS \)). Since Galena is a sulfide ore, it is concentrated using the Froth Flotation Process, which exploits the difference in surface properties between ore particles and impurities.
Step 1: Crushed galena is mixed with water in a large tank to form a slurry.
Step 2: A small amount of pine oil (or similar collector) and a frothing agent are added.
Step 3: Compressed air is blown through the mixture, creating bubbles.
Step 4: The oil selectively coats the sulfide ore particles, making them hydrophobic (water-repelling). These oil-coated particles attach to the air bubbles and rise to the surface as a stable froth.
Step 5: The froth, rich in concentrated galena, is skimmed off. The heavier gangue (silica, clay) remains submerged in the water. This method efficiently separates valuable sulfide ores from worthless impurities.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Is it possible to extract metal from the ores of element ‘A’ and ‘B’ by applying same method of extraction? Analyze with logics.","marks":4,"answer":"Comparison of Extraction Methods for A and B:
Element A is Aluminum (\( Al \)) from Bauxite. Element B is Zinc (\( Zn \)) from Calamine (\( ZnCO_3 \)). They cannot be extracted using the same method due to their positions in the reactivity series.
Aluminum Extraction: Aluminum is highly reactive and sits above carbon in the electrochemical series. Carbon is not strong enough to reduce aluminum oxide. Therefore, aluminum is extracted via electrolysis of molten alumina in cryolite, which requires substantial electrical energy to force the non-spontaneous reduction.
Zinc Extraction: Zinc is moderately reactive and lies below carbon. This allows it to be extracted economically using carbon reduction. First, calamine is calcined to form zinc oxide:
\( ZnCO_3 \rightarrow ZnO + CO_2 \)
Then, zinc oxide is heated with coke:
\( ZnO + C \rightarrow Zn + CO \)
Because their chemical reactivities differ drastically, the energy requirements and chemical reducing agents must differ. Using carbon for aluminum would fail, and using electrolysis for zinc would be unnecessarily expensive. Thus, different methods are scientifically and economically mandatory.
---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is sublimation?","marks":1,"answer":"Sublimation is a phase transition process where a solid substance changes directly into a gas (vapor) upon heating, completely bypassing the liquid state. When the vapor is cooled, it solidifies again without becoming liquid. This occurs because the substance's vapor pressure exceeds atmospheric pressure before reaching its melting point. Common examples include dry ice (\( CO_2 \)), iodine (\( I_2 \)), and ammonium chloride (\( NH_4Cl \)).","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Radioactive isotope is important in medical science. Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Medical Importance of Radioactive Isotopes: Radioisotopes emit radiation (alpha, beta, or gamma rays) as they decay. In medicine, this energy is harnessed for precise diagnosis and targeted therapy:
1. Diagnosis/Imaging: Gamma-emitting isotopes like Technetium-99m (\( ^{99m}Tc \)) are used as tracers in PET and SPECT scans. They accumulate in specific organs, allowing doctors to visualize blood flow, organ function, and detect tumors non-invasively.
2. Cancer Therapy (Radiotherapy): Cobalt-60 (\( ^{60}Co \)) and Iodine-131 (\( ^{131}I \)) deliver high-energy radiation directly to cancer cells. The radiation damages the DNA of rapidly dividing tumor cells, causing them to die while sparing most healthy tissue.
3. Treatment & Sterilization: Strontium-89 (\( ^{89}Sr \)) relieves severe bone pain from cancer metastases. Radioisotopes like Cobalt-60 are also used to sterilize surgical instruments by destroying bacteria and viruses without heat damage.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Describe the extraction of metal ‘Q’ with chemical equations.","marks":3,"answer":"Extraction of Metal Q (Calcium):
Given Earth's crust abundance (increasing order) and P (\( K \), atomic number 19), Q is logically Calcium (\( Ca \), atomic number 20), and R is likely Aluminum or Iron. Calcium is a highly reactive alkaline earth metal. It is extracted from its chloride or oxide ores using electrolysis of molten salts. For example, from fused calcium chloride (\( CaCl_2 \)):
At cathode (reduction): \( Ca^{2+} + 2e^- \rightarrow Ca(l) \)
At anode (oxidation): \( 2Cl^- \rightarrow Cl_2(g) + 2e^- \)
The process requires high temperatures to keep the salt molten and a significant electric current. The calcium metal collects at the cathode and is stored under oil to prevent reaction with air or moisture.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Discuss the process to make daily usable instruments long lasting which are made by metal ‘R’ of the stem.","marks":4,"answer":"Making Metal R (Aluminum) Instruments Long-Lasting:
Assuming R is Aluminum (high crust abundance), it naturally forms a thin oxide layer, but daily instruments require enhanced protection. Key preservation methods include:
1. Anodizing: The aluminum object is made the anode in an electrolytic cell with dilute sulfuric acid. Passing current thickens the natural \( Al_2O_3 \) layer significantly. This hard, porous coating can be dyed and sealed, making the surface highly resistant to corrosion, scratches, and wear.
2. Alloying: Mixing aluminum with copper, magnesium, or zinc (e.g., Duralumin) drastically increases its tensile strength and hardness without adding significant weight.
3. Protective Coatings: Applying non-reactive paints, polymers, or powder coatings creates a physical barrier against moisture, oxygen, and corrosive salts.
4. Cathodic Protection: In marine or industrial environments, aluminum is sometimes coupled with a more reactive "sacrificial metal" like zinc, which corrodes first, preserving the aluminum structure.
---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is ore?","marks":1,"answer":"An ore is a naturally occurring solid material from which a valuable metal or mineral can be extracted profitably and efficiently using current technological and economic methods. Not all minerals are ores; an ore must contain a sufficient concentration of the desired element, be accessible for mining, and be processable at a cost lower than the market value of the extracted metal.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Metal extraction is a reduction method—Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Extraction as Reduction: In nature, highly reactive metals do not exist in their pure metallic form because they readily combine with oxygen, sulfur, or carbonates. They exist as ores in the form of positive ions (cations) within compounds. To obtain the pure metal, these cations must gain electrons to return to their neutral, zero-oxidation state. The process of gaining electrons is called reduction. Therefore, metallurgy fundamentally relies on reducing agents like carbon, aluminum, or electric current to strip oxygen/sulfur away and force metal ions to accept electrons:
\( M^{n+} + ne^- \rightarrow M \)
Without reduction, the metal would remain locked in its compound form indefinitely.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Determine the position of Y in the periodic table.","marks":3,"answer":"Position of Y (Zinc) in Periodic Table:
Brass is an alloy of Copper (65%) and Zinc (35%). Thus, Y is Zinc (\( Zn \)). Its atomic number is 30.
Electron configuration: \( 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 3d^{10} 4s^2 \)
Period: The highest principal energy level containing electrons is 4. Therefore, Zinc belongs to Period 4.
Group: Zinc's outermost electrons are in the 4s and 3d subshells. For d-block elements where the d-subshell is complete, the group number is calculated as \( 10 + \) (electrons in outermost s). Here, \( 4s^2 \) gives 2 electrons. So, group = \( 10 + 2 \) = Group 12. Zinc is a transition metal (specifically, a post-transition metal in some classifications) located in Period 4, Group 12.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"The extraction method of X and Y metals are different—Analyze.","marks":4,"answer":"Different Extraction Methods for X (Al) and Y (Zn):
Duralumin contains ~95% Aluminum (\( Al \)). X is Aluminum, Y is Zinc. Their extraction methods differ fundamentally due to reactivity:
Aluminum Extraction (Electrolysis): Aluminum is extremely reactive and lies high in the reactivity series. Chemical reducing agents like carbon cannot pull oxygen away from \( Al_2O_3 \). Therefore, it requires electrolytic reduction of molten alumina dissolved in cryolite. This forces the reaction using electrical energy:
\( 2Al_2O_3 \rightarrow 4Al + 3O_2 \)
Zinc Extraction (Carbon Reduction): Zinc is moderately reactive and sits below carbon in the reactivity series. After roasting zinc blende to \( ZnO \), simple heating with coke (carbon) at high temperatures successfully reduces it:
\( ZnO + C \rightarrow Zn + CO \)
Using electrolysis for zinc would be economically wasteful since carbon reduction is cheap, efficient, and chemically sufficient. Conversely, using carbon for aluminum is chemically impossible. Thus, reactivity dictates the industrial pathway.
---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is called exothermic reaction?","marks":1,"answer":"An exothermic reaction is a chemical process that releases energy, usually in the form of heat, light, or sound, into its surroundings. During the reaction, the total energy of the products is lower than the total energy of the reactants. This excess energy is expelled, causing the reaction container or environment to become warmer. A common example is combustion (burning wood) or mixing acid with water.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"NaOH is strong electrolytes—Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"NaOH as a Strong Electrolyte: Electrolytes are substances that conduct electricity when dissolved in water because they dissociate into mobile ions. A strong electrolyte dissociates completely (nearly 100%) into its constituent ions in aqueous solution. Sodium hydroxide (\( NaOH \)) is an ionic compound with strong ionic bonds that water molecules easily break apart. When dissolved, it instantly and fully separates:
\( NaOH(aq) \rightarrow Na^+(aq) + OH^-(aq) \)
This complete ionization creates a high concentration of free-moving ions, allowing the solution to conduct electricity exceptionally well. Therefore, NaOH is classified as a strong electrolyte (and a strong base).","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"How dehydrating acid can be prepared from B? Write with equations.","marks":3,"answer":"Preparation of Dehydrating Acid from B (SO₂):
Gas B is Sulfur Dioxide (\( SO_2 \)), which forms sulfurous acid in water. To get the powerful dehydrating acid (Sulfuric Acid, \( H_2SO_4 \)), \( SO_2 \) must be oxidized. This is done via the Contact Process:
Step 1: Catalytic oxidation of \( SO_2 \) to sulfur trioxide (\( SO_3 \)):
\( 2SO_2(g) + O_2(g) \rightarrow 2SO_3(g) \)
Step 2: Absorption of \( SO_3 \) in concentrated \( H_2SO_4 \) to form oleum (safe handling):
\( H_2SO_4(l) + SO_3(g) \rightarrow H_2S_2O_7(l) \)
Step 3: Careful dilution of oleum with water:
\( H_2S_2O_7(l) + H_2O(l) \rightarrow 2H_2SO_4(l) \)
The final product, concentrated \( H_2SO_4 \), has a strong dehydrating nature, capable of removing water molecules from carbohydrates, alcohols, and salts.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Compare diffusion rate of gas A and B.","marks":4,"answer":"Diffusion Rate Comparison of A and B:
From the reactions: A is Carbon Dioxide (\( CO_2 \)), B is Sulfur Dioxide (\( SO_2 \)).
Molar mass of \( CO_2 \) = \( 12 + (16 \times 2) = 44 \text{ g/mol} \)
Molar mass of \( SO_2 \) = \( 32 + (16 \times 2) = 64 \text{ g/mol} \)
Graham's Law states that lighter gases diffuse faster. Since \( CO_2 \) has a lower molar mass than \( SO_2 \), Carbon Dioxide will diffuse faster. The ratio is:
\( \frac{\text{Rate}_{CO_2}}{\text{Rate}_{SO_2}} \)
\( = \sqrt{\frac{64}{44}} \)
\( \approx 1.20 \)
Thus, \( CO_2 \) diffuses about 20% faster than \( SO_2 \) under identical temperature and pressure conditions.
---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is called molarity?","marks":1,"answer":"Molarity (\( M \)) is a standard unit of concentration in chemistry. It represents the number of moles of a solute dissolved in exactly one liter of the final solution. Mathematically:
\( M = \frac{\text{moles of solute}}{\text{volume of solution in liters}} \)
It is temperature-dependent because liquid volume changes with temperature.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why soap does not produce foam in hard water? Explain it.","marks":2,"answer":"Soap Failure in Hard Water: Hard water contains high concentrations of dissolved calcium (\( Ca^{2+} \)) and magnesium (\( Mg^{2+} \)) ions. Soap molecules are sodium or potassium salts of long-chain fatty acids (e.g., sodium stearate, \( C_{17}H_{35}COONa \)). When soap is added to hard water, the sodium ions are instantly displaced by calcium or magnesium ions, forming insoluble precipitates called soap scum (calcium stearate):
\( 2C_{17}H_{35}COONa + Ca^{2+} \rightarrow (C_{17}H_{35}COO)_2Ca \downarrow + 2Na^+ \)
This solid scum does not dissolve or lather. Instead, it sticks to fabrics, sinks to the bottom, and wastes soap until all hard water ions are precipitated. Only after this "waste" phase will the remaining soap produce foam.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"How the pure metallic oxide is found from the ore of element 'R'? Explain it.","marks":3,"answer":"Purification of Bauxite (Ore of R):
Element R is Aluminum. Its ore, Bauxite, contains \( Al_2O_3 \) mixed with iron oxide, silica, and clay. Pure \( Al_2O_3 \) is isolated via the Bayer Process:
1. Digestion: Crushed bauxite is heated with concentrated \( NaOH \) at \( 150-200^\circ C \). Aluminum oxide dissolves as sodium aluminate, while impurities remain solid.
\( Al_2O_3 + 2NaOH \rightarrow 2NaAlO_2 + H_2O \)
2. Filtration: Impurities are filtered out as red mud.
3. Precipitation: The clear filtrate is cooled and seeded with fresh \( Al(OH)_3 \). Sodium aluminate hydrolyzes back to aluminum hydroxide:
\( NaAlO_2 + 2H_2O \rightarrow Al(OH)_3 \downarrow + NaOH \)
4. Calcination: The precipitate is filtered, washed, and heated strongly at \( 1100^\circ C \) to drive off water, yielding pure, dry alumina:
\( 2Al(OH)_3 \rightarrow Al_2O_3 + 3H_2O \)","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"The reaction of caustic soda solutions with metallic ion of ore 'P' and 'Q' produce precipitate in different colours.—Analyze it.","marks":4,"answer":"Colored Precipitates with NaOH:
Ore P is Chalcocite (\( Cu_2S \)), containing \( Cu^{2+} \) ions. Ore Q is Hematite (\( Fe_2O_3 \)), containing \( Fe^{3+} \) ions. Caustic soda (\( NaOH \)) provides \( OH^- \) ions, which react with these metal ions to form insoluble hydroxides with distinct colors:
With Copper(II) ions:
\( Cu^{2+} + 2OH^- \rightarrow Cu(OH)_2 \downarrow \)
This forms a pale blue, gelatinous precipitate that may turn black upon heating.
With Iron(III) ions:
\( Fe^{3+} + 3OH^- \rightarrow Fe(OH)_3 \downarrow \)
This forms a reddish-brown, gelatinous precipitate.
The different colors arise because \( Cu^{2+} \) and \( Fe^{3+} \) have different electron configurations, causing them to absorb and reflect different wavelengths of visible light when coordinated with hydroxide ligands. This property is widely used in qualitative chemical analysis.
---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is called mineral?","marks":1,"answer":"A mineral is a naturally occurring, inorganic solid with a definite chemical composition and an ordered, crystalline atomic structure. Minerals are the building blocks of rocks and form through geological processes over millions of years. Examples include quartz, calcite, and halite. They are distinguished from organic substances (like coal) and man-made materials.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Cu is an electric conductor—Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Copper as a Conductor: Copper is an excellent electrical conductor due to its atomic structure and metallic bonding. Each copper atom has one valence electron in its 4s orbital. In the solid metal lattice, these outermost electrons are delocalized, meaning they are not bound to any single atom. Instead, they form a "sea of free electrons" that can move easily throughout the entire metal structure when a voltage is applied. This effortless flow of charged particles constitutes electric current. Additionally, copper's low resistance minimizes energy loss as heat, making it ideal for wiring.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Determine the lone pair electrons of compound X.","marks":3,"answer":"Lone Pairs in Compound X:
The balanced reaction is:
\( 2NH_4Cl + CaO \rightarrow 2NH_3 + CaCl_2 + H_2O \)
Thus, gas X is Ammonia (\( NH_3 \)).
Nitrogen has 5 valence electrons (\( 2s^2 2p^3 \)). In ammonia, nitrogen forms three single covalent bonds with three hydrogen atoms, using 3 of its valence electrons. This leaves 2 electrons unshared. These remaining 2 electrons form one lone pair located on the nitrogen atom. This lone pair is responsible for ammonia's basic nature, its ability to act as a Lewis base (electron donor), and its trigonal pyramidal molecular geometry.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Are the metal extraction processes from 'Y' and zinc blend same? Analyze.","marks":4,"answer":"Comparison of Extraction from Y (Ca) vs Zinc Blende:
Compound Y is Calcium Chloride (\( CaCl_2 \)). The metal extraction processes for Calcium and Zinc are fundamentally different:
Calcium Extraction: Calcium is highly reactive (alkaline earth metal). Its chloride bond is very strong, and carbon cannot reduce it. Extraction requires electrolysis of fused \( CaCl_2 \):
\( CaCl_2(l) \rightarrow Ca^{2+} + 2Cl^- \)
At cathode: \( Ca^{2+} + 2e^- \rightarrow Ca(l) \)
Zinc Extraction: Zinc is moderately reactive. Zinc blende (\( ZnS \)) is first roasted to \( ZnO \), then reduced using carbon (coke) at high temperatures:
\( ZnO + C \rightarrow Zn + CO \)
Calcium requires electricity to force reduction because it holds onto its compound ions too tightly. Zinc's weaker ionic bonds allow cheaper chemical reduction by carbon. Therefore, the processes differ due to the metals' positions in the reactivity series and the energy required to break their respective bonds.
---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is metal alloy?","marks":1,"answer":"A metal alloy is a homogeneous mixture of two or more elements, where at least one is a metal. Alloys are created by melting the components together and cooling them. The goal is to enhance specific properties like strength, hardness, corrosion resistance, or conductivity, which the pure base metal lacks. Examples include steel (iron + carbon), brass (copper + zinc), and bronze (copper + tin).","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Cyclobutane is an aromatic compound—Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Cyclobutane is NOT Aromatic: Cyclobutane (\( C_4H_8 \)) is a cyclic alkane, not an aromatic compound. To be aromatic, a molecule must satisfy Hückel's Rule: it must be cyclic, planar, fully conjugated (alternating double/single bonds allowing continuous pi-electron overlap), and contain \( 4n+2 \) π electrons. Cyclobutane has only single sigma bonds, no pi electrons, and adopts a puckered (non-planar) shape to relieve angle strain. Because it completely lacks electron delocalization and conjugated double bonds, it behaves as a typical saturated hydrocarbon and fails all aromaticity criteria.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Describe the oleum preparation from the 'X' with chemical equation.","marks":3,"answer":"Oleum Preparation from X (\( SO_2 \)):
Roasting zinc blende produces sulfur dioxide:
\( 2ZnS + 3O_2 \rightarrow 2ZnO + 2SO_2 \)
Gas X is \( SO_2 \). Oleum (\( H_2S_2O_7 \)) is prepared in two steps:
Step 1: Catalytic oxidation to \( SO_3 \):
\( 2SO_2 + O_2 \xrightarrow{V_2O_5, 450^\circ C} 2SO_3 \)
Step 2: Absorption into concentrated \( H_2SO_4 \):
\( H_2SO_4 + SO_3 \rightarrow H_2S_2O_7 \)
The product is fuming sulfuric acid (oleum), which is stable and easily transported before final dilution to produce pure acid.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Are the condensation processes of the both ores of the stem same? Analyze.","marks":4,"answer":"Condensation of Zinc Blend vs Rutile:
Zinc Blend (\( ZnS \)) is a sulfide ore. Rutile (\( TiO_2 \)) is an oxide ore. Their concentration methods differ based on physical properties:
Zinc Blend (Sulfide): Concentrated by Froth Flotation. Crushed ore is mixed with water, pine oil, and air. Sulfide particles attach to oil-coated bubbles and float as froth, while impurities sink. This exploits surface chemistry and hydrophobicity.
Rutile (Oxide): Concentrated by Gravity Separation (Hydraulic Washing). Oxide ores like rutile are denser than gangue impurities. Crushed ore is washed with a strong stream of water on a sloped table. Heavy oxide particles settle quickly, while lighter impurities wash away. This exploits density differences, not surface chemistry.
Thus, the processes are different because one relies on chemical affinity for oil, while the other relies on physical density.
---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is ore?","marks":1,"answer":"An ore is a naturally occurring rock or mineral deposit that contains a sufficiently high concentration of a valuable metal or element to make its extraction economically viable. Ores are mined and processed to isolate the target material. If the concentration is too low, it is merely a rock; if profitable to extract, it is an ore.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why is anode negative in galvanic cell? Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Anode Polarity in Galvanic Cells: In a galvanic (voltaic) cell, chemical energy spontaneously converts to electrical energy. Oxidation (loss of electrons) occurs at the anode. As metal atoms at the anode lose electrons and enter the solution as ions, they leave behind the freed electrons on the electrode itself. This accumulation of excess negative charge makes the anode negative. These electrons then flow through the external circuit to the positive cathode, where reduction occurs. Thus, the anode is negative because it is the source of electrons.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"How much gram of salt is produced if you add 10g Zn in container A? Calculate.","marks":3,"answer":"Salt Mass Calculation:
Reaction: \( Zn + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow ZnSO_4 + H_2 \)
Molar masses: Zn = 65.4 g/mol, \( ZnSO_4 \) = 161.4 g/mol
From stoichiometry, 1 mole Zn produces 1 mole \( ZnSO_4 \).
\( 65.4 \text{ g Zn} \rightarrow 161.4 \text{ g } ZnSO_4 \)
\( 10 \text{ g Zn} \rightarrow x \text{ g } ZnSO_4 \)
\( x = \frac{10 \times 161.4}{65.4} \)
\( x \approx 24.68 \text{ g} \)
Therefore, 24.68 grams of zinc sulfate salt are produced.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"What will be the nature of the mixture if two solutions of the container are mixed in the stem? Explain.","marks":4,"answer":"Mixture Nature (Acidic/Basic/Neutral):
Moles of \( H_2SO_4 \) = Molarity \(\times\) Volume(L)
\( n_A = 0.75 \times 0.250 \)
\( = 0.1875 \text{ mol} \)
Moles of NaOH = \( 0.6 \times 0.250 \)
\( = 0.15 \text{ mol} \)
Reaction stoichiometry: \( 2NaOH + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow Na_2SO_4 + 2H_2O \)
2 moles NaOH react with 1 mole \( H_2SO_4 \).
Required \( H_2SO_4 \) for 0.15 mol NaOH = \( 0.15 / 2 \)
\( = 0.075 \text{ mol} \)
Remaining \( H_2SO_4 \) = \( 0.1875 - 0.075 \)
\( = 0.1125 \text{ mol} \)
Since unreacted sulfuric acid remains in the solution, the final mixture will be acidic in nature, with a pH significantly below 7.
---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is Effusion?","marks":1,"answer":"Effusion is the process where gas molecules escape from a container through a tiny hole (pinhole) into a vacuum or region of lower pressure. Unlike diffusion (spreading through a medium), effusion specifically involves passage through an aperture smaller than the mean free path of the gas molecules. Graham's Law applies here too: lighter gases effuse faster than heavier ones.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why group (ii) elements are called coin-metal? Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Group 11 as Coinage Metals: Elements in Group 11 (formerly IB) are Copper (\( Cu \)), Silver (\( Ag \)), and Gold (\( Au \)). Historically, they have been called "coinage metals" because they were the primary materials used to mint coins across civilizations. This is due to three key properties: 1) Durability: They resist corrosion and oxidation, preserving the coin's weight and value over centuries. 2) Malleability: They can be easily stamped and shaped into coins without cracking. 3) Rarity & Value: Their natural scarcity made them trusted standards of wealth and trade.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Which ore of the stem need heat-oxidation process to form oxide? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"Heat-Oxidation (Roasting) Requirement:
Chalcocite (\( Cu_2S \)) requires heat-oxidation. Sulfide ores are thermodynamically stable and cannot be directly reduced by carbon efficiently. They must first be roasted in excess air at high temperatures (below melting point) to convert the sulfide into a metal oxide and remove sulfur as \( SO_2 \):
\( 2Cu_2S + 3O_2 \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2Cu_2O + 2SO_2 \)
Bauxite and Calamine are already oxide/carbonate ores, so they do not require oxidative roasting.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Do you think the extraction of metal of ore (ii) and (iii) are same? Write your opinion.","marks":4,"answer":"Extraction Comparison (Bauxite vs Calamine):
No, the extraction methods are fundamentally different due to metal reactivity:
Bauxite (Aluminum): Aluminum is highly reactive. It cannot be reduced by carbon. It requires energy-intensive electrolytic reduction of molten \( Al_2O_3 \) dissolved in cryolite.
Calamine (Zinc): Zinc is moderately reactive. Calamine (\( ZnCO_3 \)) is first calcined to \( ZnO \), then easily reduced using carbon (coke) at high temperatures:
\( ZnO + C \rightarrow Zn + CO \)
Aluminum needs electrical forcing; Zinc needs chemical reducing agents. Thus, industrial pathways differ completely.
---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is empirical formula?","marks":1,"answer":"The empirical formula represents the simplest whole-number ratio of all atoms present in a compound. It does not indicate the actual number of atoms or the molecular structure, only the proportional relationship. For example, hydrogen peroxide's molecular formula is \( H_2O_2 \), but its empirical formula is \( HO \). It is determined from percent composition data and experimental analysis.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why C₂H₆ is called paraffin? Explain it.","marks":2,"answer":"C₂H₆ as Paraffin: The term "paraffin" comes from Latin roots meaning "little affinity." Ethane (\( C_2H_6 \)) is an alkane containing only strong, non-polar single sigma bonds between carbon and hydrogen. These bonds are highly stable and require significant energy to break. As a result, ethane shows extremely low chemical reactivity at room temperature: it does not react with acids, bases, oxidizing agents, or reducing agents. Because of this profound lack of chemical affinity, alkanes like ethane are historically called paraffins.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Write down the condition for finding maximum no. of product—C from above stem.","marks":3,"answer":"Conditions for Maximum SO₃ Production:
Assuming product C is \( SO_3 \) from the reaction: \( 2SO_2(g) + O_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2SO_3(g) + \text{heat} \)
According to Le Chatelier’s Principle, maximum yield requires:
1. Temperature: The forward reaction is exothermic. Low temperature favors \( SO_3 \) production. However, too low slows the rate. Optimum: \( 400-450^\circ C \).
2. Pressure: Reactants have 3 moles of gas, products have 2. High pressure shifts equilibrium forward. Optimum: 1-2 atm (industrial standard balances yield with safety/cost).
3. Catalyst: Use \( V_2O_5 \) to speed up attainment of equilibrium without shifting it.
4. Excess Reactant: Using excess oxygen pushes the reaction forward.
5. Product Removal: Continuously removing \( SO_3 \) prevents reverse reaction.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Which one would be best suitable for the preparation of E from C → E and C → D → E? Analyze it.","marks":4,"answer":"Best Route to Sulfuric Acid (E):
Route 1: \( SO_3 + H_2O \rightarrow H_2SO_4 \)
Route 2: \( SO_3 + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow H_2S_2O_7 \xrightarrow{+H_2O} 2H_2SO_4 \)
Route 2 is vastly superior. Direct hydration (Route 1) causes an intensely exothermic, uncontrollable reaction that produces a fine, corrosive mist of sulfuric acid vapor. This fog cannot be condensed efficiently, poses severe health hazards, and lowers yield. Route 2 absorbs \( SO_3 \) into existing \( 98\% \) acid, forming stable oleum. This reaction is smooth, heat-manageable, and produces no mist. Subsequent controlled dilution safely yields pure, concentrated acid. Industrial safety and efficiency dictate Route 2.","image":null,"image_url":null}]

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is electrode?","marks":1,"answer":"An electrode is a solid electrical conductor (usually a metal or graphite rod/plate) used to make contact with a non-metallic part of a circuit, such as an electrolyte solution, plasma, or vacuum. In electrochemical cells, electrodes facilitate the transfer of electrons between the external circuit and the chemical system. The anode is where oxidation occurs, and the cathode is where reduction occurs.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Explain the effect of temperature on the rate of reaction.","marks":2,"answer":"Temperature and Reaction Rate: Increasing temperature significantly increases reaction rate. Molecules possess kinetic energy; heating them makes them move faster and collide more frequently. More importantly, it increases the number of molecules that possess energy equal to or greater than the activation energy required to break bonds. According to the Arrhenius equation, even a small temperature rise can double or triple the rate because a larger fraction of collisions become effective, overcoming the energy barrier to form products.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the extraction process of the metal of ore (i).","marks":3,"answer":"Copper Extraction from Chalcocite (\( Cu_2S \)):
Chalcocite is a copper(I) sulfide ore. Extraction involves two main stages:
1. Roasting & Self-Reduction: The ore is heated in limited air. Partial oxidation converts some \( Cu_2S \) to \( Cu_2O \):
\( 2Cu_2S + 3O_2 \rightarrow 2Cu_2O + 2SO_2 \)
When heating continues in absence of excess air, the remaining \( Cu_2S \) reduces the \( Cu_2O \) to metallic copper (self-reduction):
\( Cu_2S + 2Cu_2O \rightarrow 6Cu + SO_2 \)
2. Electrolytic Refining: The crude copper (blister copper) is purified using electrolysis with \( CuSO_4 \) electrolyte. Pure copper deposits on the cathode, yielding 99.9% pure metal for electrical wiring.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"The extraction process of metal of the ore of (ii) and (iii) are different. — Justify.","marks":4,"answer":"Justification for Different Processes (Bauxite vs Hematite):
Bauxite yields Aluminum; Hematite yields Iron. Their extraction methods differ due to reactivity positions in the electrochemical series:
Aluminum (from Bauxite): Al is highly electropositive and holds oxygen very tightly. Carbon cannot reduce \( Al_2O_3 \). It requires electrolysis in molten cryolite, forcing non-spontaneous reduction via electricity.
Iron (from Hematite): Fe is moderately reactive. It sits below carbon and above hydrogen. In a blast furnace, carbon (as coke) acts as a reducing agent at high temperatures:
\( Fe_2O_3 + 3CO \rightarrow 2Fe + 3CO_2 \)
Using electricity for iron would be economically wasteful since carbon reduction is cheap and thermodynamically favorable. Conversely, using carbon for aluminum is chemically impossible. Reactivity dictates the extraction pathway.
---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is roasting?","marks":1,"answer":"Roasting is a metallurgical process where a concentrated sulfide ore is heated strongly in excess air at a temperature below its melting point. The goal is to convert the sulfide into its corresponding metal oxide, remove volatile impurities as gases, and eliminate moisture. Sulfur is driven off as sulfur dioxide (\( SO_2 \)), which is often captured to produce sulfuric acid.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Ethene is more reactive than ethane.— Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Ethene vs Ethane Reactivity: Ethane (\( C_2H_6 \)) contains only strong, stable carbon-carbon and carbon-hydrogen single sigma bonds. Electrons are tightly held between nuclei, leaving no site for attack. Ethene (\( C_2H_4 \)) contains a carbon-carbon double bond. A double bond consists of one strong sigma bond and one weaker pi bond. The pi electrons are loosely held above and below the plane of the atoms, creating an area of high electron density. This makes ethene electron-rich and highly susceptible to attack by electrophiles. Consequently, ethene readily undergoes addition reactions, while ethane requires harsh conditions (like UV light) to react.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"How will you prepare an acid which act as dehydrating agent by profitable way? Explain with equations.","marks":3,"answer":"Profitable Dehydrating Acid (\( H_2SO_4 \)) Preparation:
Element Y is Sulfur (16). The industrial Contact Process efficiently produces \( H_2SO_4 \):
1. Burn sulfur to \( SO_2 \):
\( S + O_2 \rightarrow SO_2 \)
2. Catalytically oxidize to \( SO_3 \) (exothermic, reversible, optimized at \( 450^\circ C \), 1-2 atm, \( V_2O_5 \)):
\( 2SO_2 + O_2 \rightarrow 2SO_3 \)
3. Absorb \( SO_3 \) in \( 98\% \) \( H_2SO_4 \) to form oleum:
\( H_2SO_4 + SO_3 \rightarrow H_2S_2O_7 \)
4. Dilute oleum carefully:
\( H_2S_2O_7 + H_2O \rightarrow 2H_2SO_4 \)
This indirect method prevents corrosive mists, maximizes yield, and is highly profitable due to catalyst longevity and heat recovery.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Will the extraction process of 'X' and 'Z' elements from the ores be same? Analyze with equations.","marks":4,"answer":"Extraction of X (Al) vs Z (Fe):
No, extraction methods differ fundamentally:
Aluminum (X=13): Requires electrolysis of molten \( Al_2O_3 \) in cryolite:
At cathode: \( 4Al^{3+} + 12e^- \rightarrow 4Al \)
At anode: \( 6O^{2-} \rightarrow 3O_2 + 12e^- \)
Iron (Z=26): Extracted via carbon reduction in blast furnace:
\( Fe_2O_3 + 3C \rightarrow 2Fe + 3CO \)
Aluminum's strong ionic bonds require electrical energy. Iron's weaker bonds yield to chemical reduction by carbon. Same method is impossible.
---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is called photosynthesis?","marks":1,"answer":"Photosynthesis is the biochemical process by which green plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy (usually from the sun) into chemical energy. Using chlorophyll, they absorb carbon dioxide from the air and water from the soil to synthesize glucose (\( C_6H_{12}O_6 \)) and release oxygen (\( O_2 \)) as a byproduct. It is the foundation of almost all life on Earth, providing food and atmospheric oxygen.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why is ripened mango sweet in taste? Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Sweetness of Ripe Mangoes: Unripe mangoes contain high concentrations of organic acids (like citric, malic, and tartaric acid) and complex starches, giving a sour, firm taste. During ripening, enzymes break down starches into simple sugars (glucose, fructose, sucrose). Simultaneously, organic acids are metabolized or diluted, and new volatile aromatic compounds are synthesized. The shift from acid/starch dominance to sugar dominance, combined with softer pectin breakdown, creates the characteristic sweet, fragrant profile of ripe mangoes.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Show the preparation of the compound 'A' by giving chemical reactions.","marks":3,"answer":"Preparation of Compound A (\( H_2SO_4 \)):
Balancing the stem: \( Zn + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow ZnSO_4 + H_2 \)
So A is Sulfuric Acid. Prepared via Contact Process:
1. \( S + O_2 \rightarrow SO_2 \)
2. \( 2SO_2 + O_2 \xrightarrow{V_2O_5, 450^\circ C} 2SO_3 \)
3. \( H_2SO_4 + SO_3 \rightarrow H_2S_2O_7 \)
4. \( H_2S_2O_7 + H_2O \rightarrow 2H_2SO_4 \)","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Compound 'A' is an acid having oxidation property. Justify it with reactions.","marks":4,"answer":"Oxidation Property of A:
Concentrated \( H_2SO_4 \) is a strong oxidizing agent. It decomposes to release atomic oxygen (\( [O] \)), which oxidizes metals, carbon, and sulfur. For copper:
\( H_2SO_4(\text{conc}) \rightarrow H_2O + SO_2 + [O] \)
\( Cu + [O] \rightarrow CuO \)
\( CuO + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow CuSO_4 + H_2O \)
Overall: \( Cu + 2H_2SO_4 \rightarrow CuSO_4 + SO_2 + 2H_2O \)
Copper's oxidation state increases from 0 to +2, while sulfur's decreases from +6 to +4. This electron transfer confirms \( H_2SO_4 \)'s oxidizing nature.
